a cunning plan: The thieves came up with a cunning plan to trick the guards and steal the diamond without being seen.
竊賊們想出一個狡詐的計畫，要騙過警衛並在不被發現的情況下偷走鑽石。
a cunning device: The inventor showed us a cunning device that opens the window automatically when the room gets too hot.
發明家向我們展示了一個巧妙的裝置，當房間太熱時會自動打開窗戶。
as cunning as a fox: The old businessman is as cunning as a fox, and he always finds a way to win every deal.
那位老商人像狐狸一樣狡猾，他總能找到方法談成每筆生意。
a damp squib: The fireworks show we had waited for all year turned out to be a damp squib because of the heavy rain.
我們等了一整年的煙火秀因為大雨，結果成了令人失望的一場。
damp weather: In damp weather, our clothes never dry properly, and black spots of mold start to grow on the walls.
在潮濕的天氣裡，我們的衣服總是乾不透，牆上也開始長出黑色的霉斑。
put a damper on: The sudden thunderstorm put a damper on our beach picnic, so we packed up and went home early.
突如其來的雷雨使我們的海灘野餐興致大減，所以我們收拾東西提早回家了。
a deadly weapon: In the hands of a careless driver, a car can become a deadly weapon that kills innocent people.
在粗心的駕駛手中，汽車可能變成殺害無辜民眾的致命武器。
deadly serious: He laughed at first, but then I realized he was deadly serious about quitting his job to travel the world.
他起初笑了，但後來我發現他對辭職去環遊世界是極度認真的。
a deadly silence: After the teacher announced that nobody had passed the test, a deadly silence fell over the whole classroom.
老師宣布沒有人通過考試後，整間教室陷入一片死寂。
deadly enemies: The two families had been deadly enemies for years, and their children were not even allowed to speak to each other.
這兩個家族多年來一直是死敵，他們的孩子甚至不被允許和對方說話。
be deadly dull: The speech was deadly dull, and half of the audience fell asleep before the speaker reached his second point.
那場演講無聊至極，一半的聽眾在講者講到第二點之前就睡著了。
a decent salary: She finally found a job with a decent salary, so she can pay her rent and still save some money.
她終於找到一份薪水體面的工作，所以她可以付房租，還能存一些錢。
a decent meal: After a week of eating instant noodles while camping, we were happy to have a decent meal at a restaurant.
露營時吃了一週的泡麵後，我們很高興能在餐廳吃上像樣的一餐。
do the decent thing: The boy admitted that he had broken the window and offered to pay for it; he did the decent thing.
那男孩承認是他打破窗戶，並主動提出賠償；他做了正當的事。
decent people: Most of our neighbors are decent people who would return a lost wallet without taking any of the money.
我們大多數的鄰居都是正派的人，撿到遺失的錢包會原封不動地歸還。
a decent night's sleep: The baby cried all night, so his parents have not had a decent night's sleep for almost a week.
寶寶整晚哭鬧，所以他的父母已經將近一週沒有好好睡一晚了。
be on the defensive: After the reporter asked about the missing money, the mayor was on the defensive and refused to answer clearly.
記者問到那筆不見的錢之後，市長處於防衛狀態，拒絕清楚回答。
a defensive attitude: He always takes a defensive attitude when his parents ask about his grades, as if they were attacking him.
每當父母問起他的成績，他總是採取防衛性的態度，好像他們在攻擊他一樣。
defensive driving: The driving school teaches defensive driving, so students learn to expect other drivers' mistakes and avoid accidents.
這所駕訓班教防禦性駕駛，讓學員學會預料其他駕駛的錯誤並避免事故。
get defensive: Whenever someone points out a mistake in his work, he gets defensive and starts making excuses instead of listening.
每當有人指出他工作上的錯誤，他就變得急著為自己辯護，開始找藉口而不是好好聽。
a definite answer: I asked my boss whether I could take next Friday off, but she hasn't given me a definite answer yet.
我問老闆下週五能不能請假，但她還沒給我明確的答覆。
a definite improvement: Your handwriting shows a definite improvement since last month; your teacher can finally read your essays easily.
你的字跡從上個月起有了明顯的改善；你的老師終於能輕鬆閱讀你的作文了。
the definite article: In English, we use the definite article "the" when both the speaker and listener know which thing we mean.
在英文中，當說話者和聽者都知道我們指的是哪個東西時，我們會使用定冠詞「the」。
for definite: I can't say for definite whether I'll come to the party, because I might have to work that night.
我無法確定地說我會不會來參加派對，因為那天晚上我可能得上班。
a deliberate attempt: The fake news story was a deliberate attempt to mislead voters just a few days before the election.
那則假新聞是在選舉前幾天蓄意誤導選民的企圖。
a deliberate lie: It wasn't a simple mistake; he told a deliberate lie to cover up the fact that he had skipped class.
那不是單純的失誤；他故意說謊，以掩飾他翹課的事實。
speak in a slow, deliberate way: When she is angry, my mother speaks in a slow, deliberate way, pausing calmly between words so we know she means it.
我媽媽生氣時會慢而從容地說話，字與字之間冷靜地停頓，讓我們知道她是認真的。
a deliberate insult: Not inviting his own brother to the wedding was seen as a deliberate insult by the whole family.
沒邀請自己的哥哥參加婚禮，被全家人視為故意的侮辱。
